Disaster-recovery or emergency utility backup project with a named buyer: one search. Results were DoD resilience programs (Janus, ANPI), already in deployment_sites. Nothing utility-named.
Signed 2026 deal for a 1 MW microreactor pilot with an off-grid industrial customer: none found. Terra Innovatum / Uvation (LOI, Nov 2025) is already shipped as uvation-data-center-pilot.

Faroe Islands region (Type E): only price data found was 2019-2020 (DKK 1.31/kWh) and no nuclear activity. Rejected under the price-and-load rule. No 2026 SEV tariff page reached.

applications.name: USNC, Hyundai Engineering and SK E&C Hydrogen Micro Hub, Seoul
applications.power_class: 5 MWe (15 MWth) per USNC Micro-Modular Reactor
applications.timeline: MOU signed 2023-04-20 (ANS); WNN reported 2023-04-21; five-year joint R&D; no project update after 2023 found
applications.vendor: Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (MMR); Hyundai Engineering (balance of plant and EPC)
applications.what_it_says: USNC, Hyundai Engineering and SK E&C signed an MOU in April 2023 to build a Hydrogen Micro Hub that makes hydrogen by high-temperature electrolysis, fed by electricity and steam from USNC's 5 MWe Micro-Modular Reactor. The first hub was to be built at SK E&C's Seoul headquarters. No project update after 2023 was found, and ANS lists a related headline reporting that USNC filed for bankruptcy on 2024-10-30.
applications.microreactor_read: A 5 MWe block sits inside the 1-20 MW band and makes hydrogen-grade heat, but the design vendor is in bankruptcy and no site, buyer commitment or price is published.

applications.name: Hadron Energy and Smartland Energy Halo microreactor framework (non-binding MOU)
applications.power_class: 10 MWe per Halo unit; up to five units under the MOU
applications.timeline: MOU announced 2026-04-28; initial deployment targeted for the early 2030s, subject to diligence and definitive agreements
applications.sponsor: Smartland Energy (behind-the-meter developer; made an initial strategic investment in Hadron)
applications.what_it_says: Hadron Energy and Smartland Energy signed a non-binding MOU on 2026-04-28 to evaluate Halo reactors across up to five Smartland projects. Smartland describes a pipeline of about 150 MWe per project, with 12 projects targeted by 2035 for about 1.8 GWe of demand. No project site has been publicly identified, and the release says no existing Smartland project has been selected for nuclear deployment.
applications.microreactor_read: 10 MWe fits the 1-20 MW band. The MOU is non-binding, no site or price is named, and initial deployment is pushed to the early 2030s.
